xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-5093: Alert the operator (Needs-you + phone push) when free disk drops below 5 GiB / 2 GiB; today it hit 17 MB unnoticed

plan.title: Alert the operator (Needs-you + phone push) when free disk drops below 5 GiB / 2 GiB; today it hit 17 MB unnoticed
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

metadata.sizeJustification: One alert feature fed by one state machine: the issue requires both the Needs-you item and the phone push, and splitting the dashboard card into a sibling issue would ship a disk alert API with no on-screen consumer. The 33-file surface is 8 small items, 13 of whose files are new tests or the CI test-subset list; the subsystem count is inflated because each of the three doc files counts as its own subsystem. Every item runs in its own slot with no shared files.

narratives.Problem: Free space on / fell from 7.5 GiB to 17 MB within an hour on 2026-11-06 and nothing told the operator. At that level SQLite and transcript JSONL writes can fail mid-write and zero-fill files. The only disk guards today hold new workspace setups below 10 GiB (src/lib/disk-floor.ts, PAN-4961) and prune Docker BuildKit cache (src/lib/cloister/disk-pressure-patrol.ts, PAN-3809); neither raises a Needs-you item or a phone push.
narratives.Proposal: A disk alert service in the primary dashboard polls statfs on the Overdeck home every 30 s. A pure state machine (src/lib/disk-alert.ts) moves between ok, warning (below resources.disk_warn_gb, default 5) and critical (below resources.disk_critical_gb, default 2), raising at once and lowering only 0.5 GiB past a threshold. Each upward crossing sends one edge push through the existing needs-you dispatcher (kind failed, tag disk:<level>:<since>) and writes an activity entry, then measures the biggest space holders once (du with 120 s timeouts, Docker reclaimable, the conversation search index). GET /api/disk-alert serves the snapshot; useDecisions turns it into one Needs-you item (diskLow, or blocking diskCritical) rendered by a dedicated DiskAlertCard on the desktop and a read-only line on the phone. Docs: docs/PIPELINE-GATES.md, configuration/memory-governor.mdx, configuration/push-notifications.mdx. Full detail and before/after code in .pan/drafts/PAN-5093.md.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Deleting, pruning, migrating or moving any file or directory; the holder list is read-only, including the stale ~/.overdeck/conversations/embeddings.db copy
- Changing DISK_SAFETY_FLOOR_BYTES, DISK_PRUNE_TRIGGER_BYTES, the BuildKit prune patrol or hygiene.ts's 10 GiB default, or unifying them with the new keys
- A new push kind, a new phone notification category, or any change under apps/mobile
- Raising ntfy priority, or bypassing the push rate limit, pause or category mute
- Propagating the disk alert to linked machines (buildNeedsYou() and the fleet Needs-you stay unchanged)
- Watching any filesystem other than the one holding the Overdeck home
- A Settings UI for the thresholds
- Running the alert in the Deacon child, behind the Deacon freeze, or in a CLI command
- Running du or docker on every poll

autoDecisions.summary: Run the alert as a primary-dashboard service, not a Deacon patrol
autoDecisions.rationale: The push dispatcher lives in the primary dashboard process; a Deacon patrol would need a new cross-process event, and the Deacon freeze would silence the alert exactly when nobody is watching. This also settles the issue's TENET-10 note: nothing goes into the Deacon patrol, so no supervised handoff is needed.

autoDecisions.summary: Reuse push kind 'failed' and category 'failed' instead of adding a kind or category
autoDecisions.rationale: The dispatcher drops kinds missing from an explicit push.events list, and a new phone category is a key of the phone app's closed CATEGORY_LABEL record, needing an app release. Consequence: a phone with Failures muted or paused gets no disk push; the Needs-you item still shows.

autoDecisions.summary: 'Louder' critical = its own push titled 'Disk critical', plus a blocking Needs-you item sorted first
autoDecisions.rationale: Web Push and the Overdeck app already send failed at high urgency. Raising ntfy priority would widen the provider surface for a marginal gain; recorded as a NonGoal.

autoDecisions.summary: Thresholds are config keys resources.disk_warn_gb (5) and resources.disk_critical_gb (2); poll interval 30 s and recovery margin 0.5 GiB are documented constants
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue asks for config keys beside the disk floor with documented defaults; the memory keys use the *_gb naming in the same resources block. An inverted pair falls back to the defaults with one warning, matching merge-cpu.ts. Thresholds are read each poll with the async loadGlobalConfigNoMigration() (machine-wide global config), never the sync loadConfigSync().

autoDecisions.summary: A dashboard that starts while the disk is already low pushes once
autoDecisions.rationale: The incident went unnoticed; failing loud on start is the point. A restart while still low pushing again is accepted.

autoDecisions.summary: Push first, measure holders afterwards, once per crossing, 120 s per path, at most 4 du processes
autoDecisions.rationale: du over 53 GiB trees on a nearly full disk can take minutes; the push must not wait on it, and repeated du would add I/O load while the disk is under pressure.

autoDecisions.summary: Show both conversation search index files (configured and stale default path) in the holders; defer cleanup or migration
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue comment asks for the index size in the hints and a decision on the stale copy. The issue scopes hints as read-only, so the stale copy is labeled 'not in use' for the operator to judge, and cleanup is a NonGoal.

autoDecisions.summary: Keep the dispatcher's rate limit, pause and mute for disk pushes
autoDecisions.rationale: Pause and mute are explicit operator choices; at most two disk pushes per crossing make summary folding rare, and the Needs-you item still carries the details.
Server and frontend both use it; packages/contracts is the repo's shared-type home.

items.title: Add resources.disk_warn_gb and resources.disk_critical_gb config keys

narrative.Action: PRD WI-1. Create schema-disk.ts (DiskResourcesYamlConfig with disk_warn_gb/disk_critical_gb; DiskResourcesConfig with diskWarnGb/diskCriticalGb) and merge-disk.ts (mergeDiskResources(yaml, resolved, defaults): accept finite numbers > 0 and <= 1024; if critical >= warn, console.warn once per distinct pair and reset both to defaults). Extend ResourcesConfig (schema.ts line 421) with DiskResourcesYamlConfig and the resolved resources type (schema.ts line 979) with DiskResourcesConfig; add diskWarnGb: 5 and diskCriticalGb: 2 to the defaults.ts resources block; call mergeDiskResources right after mergeCpuResources in merge.ts (line 854). schema.ts must stay <= 1114 lines and merge.ts <= 1045.

items.title: Given no resources.disk_* keys, when the config merges, then resources.diskWarnGb defaults to 5 and resources.diskCriticalGb defaults to 2
Given disk_warn_gb: 8 and disk_critical_gb: 3, when merged, then the resolved values are 8 and 3; values 0, -1, '5', NaN and 2000 are ignored and the earlier value is preserved
Given disk_warn_gb: 2 and disk_critical_gb: 3, when merged twice, then both values fall back to 5 and 2 and console.warn is emitted exactly once

packages/contracts exports DiskAlertSnapshot and npm run typecheck exits 0
Add the read-only space holder collector

narrative.Action: PRD WI-3. collectDiskHolders(deps) measures each child of the Overdeck home, ~/.claude/projects, ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db, the configured conversationSearch.dbPath and (when different and present) ~/.overdeck/conversations/embeddings.db, and the caches ~/.local/share/pnpm/store, ~/.cache/huggingface, ~/.cache/ms-playwright, ~/.npm/_cacache, ~/.bun/install/cache, ~/.cache/uv. Skip missing paths and paths on a different device than the Overdeck home. Directories via async execFile('du', ['-sk','-x',path], {timeout: 120_000}) at most 4 at a time; files via stat size; a rejected measure drops the row and sets incomplete. Docker reclaimable via async 'docker system df --format {{json .}}' summed with parseDockerReclaimable (strip '(NN%)', reuse parseDockerSize from src/lib/workspace/disk-cost.ts). Sort descending, drop rows under 100 MiB, keep 12, then re-append any cut conversation index row. Labels per the PRD. All I/O injectable; no execSync. conversationIndexPath is passed in by the caller, which reads it with the async loadGlobalConfigNoMigration(), never loadConfigSync.

items.title: Given injected sizes, collectDiskHolders returns rows sorted by bytes descending, capped at 12, without rows under 100 MiB

Given a conversation index smaller than the 12th row, the result still includes a 'Conversation search index' row; a 'Conversation search index (not in use)' row appears only when the configured path differs from the default path and the default file exists
collectDiskHolders returns no row for a path whose dev differs from the Overdeck home's dev, and when duKb rejects for a path it returns the other rows with incomplete: true
parseDockerReclaimable sums the Reclaimable column of every JSON line (e.g. '1.5GB (40%)' and '500MB (10%)') using parseDockerSize, and returns 0 for empty input

metadata.acJustification: Six ACs: the critique-driven scan concurrency and recovery-invalidation cases are separate behaviors from the crossing/push rules and each needs its own check.

narrative.Action: PRD WI-4 (revised after critique round 1). Add pushNeedsYouEdge(notification) to needs-you-push-service.ts (state?.dispatcher.observeEdge; no-op before start). Create disk-alert-service.ts with startDiskAlertService(deps) (idempotent; one poll at once, then setInterval(DISK_ALERT_POLL_MS) unref'd; skip a tick while a poll is in flight), stopDiskAlertService(), getDiskAlertSnapshot() (level 'ok', checkedAt null when not started) and pollDiskAlertOnce(). Each poll: await readThresholds() — diskAlertThresholds((await loadGlobalConfigNoMigration()).config.resources), never loadConfigSync (it does sync fs reads); a rejection keeps the last good thresholds — then async statfs of getOverdeckHome() (failure -> skip, level unchanged), then nextDiskAlertLevel. On a crossing: set since, push(diskAlertPush(...)), emitActivityEntry (source 'dashboard', link '/resources', warn for warning, error + desktop:true for critical), then ensureHolderScan(). critical->warning: no push, no entry, since kept. Any->ok: clear since and holders, increment alertGeneration, emit one info entry. ensureHolderScan(): no-op while scanInFlight (one scan service-wide, so at most 4 du processes across crossings); else record scanGeneration = alertGeneration, measuring = true, run collectHolders(); on settle clear scanInFlight and measuring, publish the result (rejection -> { incomplete: true, holders: [] }) only if scanGeneration === alertGeneration and level !== 'ok'; if stale and level !== 'ok', call ensureHolderScan() again. In main.ts call startDiskAlertService() right after startNeedsYouPushService(...) inside the existing !isPeerDashboard block (line 280) and stopDiskAlertService() beside stopNeedsYouPushService() (line 779); at most 7 added lines. Tests use vi.useFakeTimers and inject every dep, with deferred promises for the collector.

items.title: Given free space 4 GiB on the first poll, the service pushes exactly one notification with tag starting 'disk:warning:' and a second poll at 4 GiB pushes nothing

Given a warning level, a poll at 1.5 GiB pushes one critical notification, a later poll at 3 GiB pushes nothing and the snapshot level becomes 'warning', and a poll at 5.6 GiB returns level 'ok' and emits one info activity entry
After a recovery to ok, a new drop to 4 GiB (advanced with vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync) pushes again with a tag different from the first warning's tag
When readSpace rejects, the level is preserved and nothing is pushed; when readThresholds rejects, the poll applies the previous thresholds

Given an unresolved collector during warning, when a critical poll follows, then collectHolders was called exactly once and its result shows on the critical snapshot; when the disk recovers to ok before the collector resolves, then the snapshot keeps holders: null; when a new crossing happens before that stale scan resolves, then collectHolders is called a second time
After stopDiskAlertService(), advancing fake time by 120 s produces no further readSpace calls, and main.ts is at or under 1000 lines
